title: The Inverse of a Square Matrix

questions.prompt: What is the definition of the inverse of a matrix $A$?
options: A. A matrix $B$ such that $A + B = I$
B. A matrix $A^{-1}$ such that $AA^{-1} = I$ and $A^{-1}A = I$
C. A matrix obtained by transposing $A$
D. A matrix with the same entries as $A$ but with opposite signs
hints: Both left and right multiplication give the identity.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The inverse satisfies $AA^{-1} = I$ and $A^{-1}A = I$.

questions.prompt: The product of a matrix and its inverse is the ___ matrix.
hints: It has 1s on the diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

questions.prompt: If $AB = I$, then $B$ is the ___ of $A$.
To find the inverse of a matrix using the Gauss‑Jordan method, you adjoin which matrix to the original?
hints: Then row reduce until the left side becomes $I$.

questions.prompt: If the determinant $ad-bc$ equals zero for a $2 \times 2$ matrix, then the matrix is ___.
What is the determinant of $\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$? (Enter a number)
Which matrix is the inverse of $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$?
To solve $AX = B$ using the inverse, you compute $X =$ ___$B$.
hints: Multiply on the left by the inverse of $A$.

questions.prompt: If $A$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix with determinant $5$, what is the determinant of $A^{-1}$? (Enter a fraction or decimal)
hints: The determinant of the inverse is the reciprocal.

questions.prompt: If a square matrix $A$ is singular, then the system $AX = B$ has:
options: B. No solution or infinitely many
hints: A singular matrix has no inverse.
The system may be inconsistent or have infinitely many solutions.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A singular matrix leads to either no solution or infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: In the $2 \times 2$ inverse formula, the entry that was originally $b$ (top-right) becomes ___ in the adjugate (before multiplying by $1/det$).
Given $A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, what is $(A^{-1})^{-1}$? (Enter the matrix as [a,b;c,d])
hints: The inverse of the inverse is the original matrix.
What matrix has an inverse of $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$? Its inverse is $\begin{bmatrix} 1/2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/3 \end{bmatrix}$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The inverse of $A^{-1}$ is $A$, which is $\begin{bmatrix} 1/2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/3 \end{bmatrix}$.

questions.prompt: To check if $B$ is the inverse of $A$, you must verify that:
hints: However, for square matrices, one implies the other, but the definition includes both.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: You need both $AB = I$ and $BA = I$ (though for square matrices one is enough, the definition says both).

questions.prompt: When row reducing $[A \mid I]$ to find $A^{-1}$, the operations must be applied to the ___ rows.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: You must apply the operation to the entire row (both sides of the vertical line).
